c.tagline: Sri Lanka's east-coast harbour city of clifftop temples and calm blue beaches.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis are rare; PickMe and Uber operate but with limited coverage in Trincomalee. Most short trips are by three-wheeler (tuk-tuk) - agree the fare before setting off or ask the driver to use the PickMe app meter.

emergency.note: 119/118 reach the police; 110 is fire and rescue, and 1990 is the free nationwide Suwa Seriya ambulance service.

avoid.reason: Avoid isolated stretches of Uppuveli and Nilaveli beaches after dark and expect persistent touts around the bus stand and temple.

hood_desc: The compact city centre on a harbour peninsula, crowned by Fort Frederick and the clifftop Koneswaram Temple on Swami Rock; the practical base for markets, transport, and sights.
A relaxed beach village about 6 km north of town with a long sandy bay, guesthouses, and seafood cafes; the most popular base for beach-goers and backpackers.
A quieter stretch of wide white-sand beach roughly 16 km north, home to the area's resorts and the jumping-off point for snorkeling and diving at Pigeon Island National Park.
A small sheltered bay and promenade right by the town centre, popular with locals at sunset and lined with a few guesthouses; convenient and central.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; avoid tap water and ice of unknown origin.

sys.n: Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) & private buses

transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the conductor in small rupee notes; train tickets are bought at the station counter. There is no rechargeable transit card. Within town and to the northern beaches, hired three-wheelers (tuk-tuks) are the usual way to get around - agree the fare first or use the PickMe app.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5am-8pm with sparse evening service, and the trains to and from Colombo and the eastern line run limited daily schedules. After dark, tuk-tuks and ride apps are the norm.
transit.note: Trincomalee has no metro or tram; buses, tuk-tuks, and a limited rail line are the transport options, and a hired tuk-tuk or car with driver is the easiest way to reach Uppuveli, Nilaveli, and Pigeon Island.

train: Sri Lanka Railways - Trincomalee line (via Gal Oya junction to Colombo)

car.idp: Required (with a temporary Sri Lankan permit)

transit.m: Tuk-tuk to town or Uppuveli (25-35 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a 10% service charge is often added at hotels and restaurants, and rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated.

food.name: Crab curry
food.desc: Lagoon and sea crab simmered in dark roasted Jaffna curry powder with coconut milk, fenugreek and tamarind. Eaten with rice or pittu, and with your hands.

places.name: King Fish Seafood
places.note: Cheap seafood kitchen where regulars order the crab and prawn curries.

places.name: Dutch Bank Cafe
places.note: Colonial-era building in town serving Tamil-style seafood curries and rice plates.

places.name: Trinco Blu by Cinnamon
places.note: Long-established beach hotel whose kitchen does a reliable, less fiery crab curry.

food.name: Odiyal kool
food.desc: The great northeastern seafood broth: crab, prawn, cuttlefish and fish thickened with palmyrah root flour into a thick, peppery, red-hot soup.

places.name: Anna Pooram Restaurant
places.note: Local Tamil kitchen in town; ask about kool, which is often made to order or on weekends.

places.name: Dutch Bank Cafe
places.note: One of the few tourist-friendly places in town cooking regional Tamil specialities.

places.name: Shami Seafood Restaurant
places.note: Fresh-catch seafood kitchen; ask in the morning if you want kool, which is cooked to order.

food.name: Grilled and devilled seafood
food.desc: Seer fish steaks, king prawns, cuttlefish and lobster from the morning boats, grilled over coals or fried devilled with onion, chilli and soy.

places.name: Trinco Lanka Restaurant
places.note: Beachside kitchen grilling the day's catch, a few steps from the sand.

places.name: Nilaveli Beach Hotel
places.note: One of the coast's oldest hotels; seafood grill on the sand near Pigeon Island.

places.name: Trinco Blu by Cinnamon
places.note: Beachside barbecue nights with the day's catch, dependable for nervous stomachs.

food.name: Kottu roti
food.desc: Godamba roti chopped on a hot griddle with egg, vegetables and chicken or seafood, the clatter of the blades audible down the street.

places.name: Trincomalee town street stalls
places.note: Evening kottu shops fire up after dark; follow the sound of the metal blades.

places.name: Anna Pooram Restaurant
places.note: Straightforward town kitchen doing cheap vegetable and egg kottu for locals.

places.name: Dutch Bay food stalls
places.note: Beachfront carts sell kottu and short eats to families in the evenings.

food.name: Hoppers and string hoppers
food.desc: Bowl-shaped fermented rice-flour appam with a soft egg in the middle, or steamed idiyappam nests, eaten with coconut sambol, dhal and sothi gravy.

places.name: Anna Pooram Restaurant
places.note: Reliable South Indian and Sri Lankan breakfasts; hoppers appear morning and evening.

places.name: Trincomalee town street stalls
places.note: Hopper pans come out at dusk; buy them by the piece, hottest straight from the pan.

places.name: Trinco Blu by Cinnamon
places.note: Hopper station at breakfast, cooked to order alongside the buffet.

food.name: Rice and curry, Tamil style
food.desc: A plate of red rice ringed by small curries: dhal, jackfruit, snake gourd, dried fish, mango and a fierce pol sambol of scraped coconut and chilli.

places.name: Anna Pooram Restaurant
places.note: Vegetarian rice-and-curry plates at local prices; busiest at lunchtime.

places.name: Dutch Bank Cafe
places.note: Sit-down lunch plates with a wide spread of curries in a historic town building.

places.name: Trincomalee Central Market
places.note: Cook-shops around the market feed traders cheap rice and curry from mid-morning.

food.name: Thambili (king coconut)
food.desc: Orange king coconut hacked open with a knife and drunk through the top; sweeter and more mineral than green coconut water, and sold everywhere.

places.name: Trincomalee Central Market
places.note: Cartloads of king coconut for a few rupees; the vendor opens it in front of you.

places.name: Dutch Bay food stalls
places.note: Coconut carts line the seafront promenade, busiest in the late afternoon.

places.name: Fort Frederick approach road
places.note: Vendors work the walk up to Koneswaram temple, a welcome stop in the heat.

food.name: Palmyrah toddy and arrack
food.desc: Sap tapped from palmyrah palms and left to ferment into cloudy, sour toddy, or distilled into arrack, usually drunk long with soda and lime.

places.name: Uppuveli beach bars
places.note: Bars along the Uppuveli strip pour arrack with soda and lime at sundown.

places.name: Trinco Blu by Cinnamon
places.note: Hotel bar with coconut and palmyrah arrack cocktails overlooking the bay.

places.name: Nilaveli Beach Hotel
places.note: Old-school hotel bar; arrack with king coconut or soda after a day on the sand.

landmarks: Koneswaram Temple
Perched atop Swami Rock's sheer cliffs, this ancient Shiva temple of a Thousand Pillars fame blazes with colour above the deep blue of Trincomalee Bay.
Fort Frederick
Walk through this 17th-century Portuguese-Dutch-British fortress, still garrisoned and roamed by deer, en route up Swami Rock to Koneswaram's sacred promontory.
Nilaveli Beach
Sri Lanka's archetypal east-coast beach stretches pale and palm-fringed for kilometres, with calm seas ideal for swimming, diving and long barefoot walks.
Uppuveli Beach
Closer to town than Nilaveli, this relaxed golden strand mixes beach bars and fishing boats with gentle surf and glorious sunrise views.
Swami Rock and Lover's Leap
The 130-metre cliff behind Koneswaram, ringed by legends of a Dutch maiden's leap, offers dizzying ocean views and seasonal blue-whale sightings.
Kanniya Hot Springs
Seven ancient wells of varying temperatures, linked to Ravana legends, invite visitors to douse themselves with bucket after bucket of therapeutic warm water.
Marble Beach
Managed by the Sri Lankan Air Force, this immaculate cove's glass-clear water and marble-smooth sand make it Trincomalee's most pristine swimming spot.
Trincomalee War Cemetery
Immaculately tended graves of over 350 Commonwealth servicemen from World War II rest beneath frangipani trees, a moving memorial near Uppuveli.
Dutch Bay Beach
A golden-sand beach a few kilometers from the harbor, named for its role as a Dutch colonial anchorage, where wild deer wander the shoreline at dusk.
Trincomalee Harbour
One of the world's largest natural deep-water harbors, a curving bay that has drawn traders and navies since antiquity and still frames the city's waterfront.

train.note: Sri Lanka Railways runs day and overnight trains between Trincomalee and Colombo (about 8-9 hrs) via Maho/Gal Oya junction; there are no international rail links (Sri Lanka is an island).

bus.note: SLTB and private intercity buses connect Trincomalee with Colombo (~6-7 hrs), Kandy, Anuradhapura, and Batticaloa; there are no international bus routes.

ferry.note: Trincomalee has one of the world's finest natural deep-water harbours but no scheduled passenger ferry service; it is used by the navy and cargo shipping.

half.name: Pigeon Island National Park
half.blurb: A tiny coral island off Nilaveli with snorkeling among reef fish and blacktip reef sharks, reached by a short boat ride.

half.name: Velgam Vehera
half.blurb: An evocative ancient Buddhist monastery near Periyakulam tank, venerated by both Sinhalese and Tamils, with a restored dagoba amid centuries-old ruins.

full.name: Anuradhapura
full.blurb: Sri Lanka's ancient sacred city of vast dagobas and ruins, a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 2-3 hrs inland.

full.name: Sigiriya
full.blurb: The iconic 5th-century rock fortress with frescoes and a lion-paw stairway, a long day trip southwest.

full.name: Polonnaruwa
full.blurb: Medieval royal capital with well-preserved stupas, statues, and stone carvings.
